answer: Hold every scenario input except the candidate configuration identical. Candidates must run at the same offered arrival rate; the worked checkout comparison holds lambda at 20 requests per second for candidates A, B and C. They must share the same serving capacity and queueing boundary: capacity 24 with the declared admission, bounded queue, server pool, per-attempt deadlines and bounded retries, otherwise success, p95 and timeout differences measure different systems. Model and scenario identity must be pinned by hash: the run stores the SHA-256 of the model file and of its scenario file, and replay fails before producing a new number if either changes. Engine and sampling context must be recorded and held constant: engine name and version, deterministic flag, seed base, replication count and input hash are required provenance. Metric and candidate binding must be identical: each metric records identifier, unit, direction and a business-comparable flag, and each candidate entry names its scenario, run set and owner pages within one decision record. Boundaries: alignment is necessary, not sufficient - inputs are synthetic and the model uncalibrated, so narrow intervals are sampling precision, not measured inputs. A different workload is allowed only as a declared workload family. Equal replication counts are not stated as a hard rule, and no mechanical cross-candidate equality gate is demonstrated.
